title: Pulled Pork
subtitle: Slow-roasted pork shoulder with a smoky spice rub
excerpt: Pork shoulder rubbed with smoked paprika, cumin, and brown sugar, roasted low and slow for hours until the meat pulls apart into tender, juicy shreds. Served in buns with coleslaw.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pulled pork is a dish of American barbecue, particularly associated with the Carolinas, Tennessee, and the American South. In its traditional form it is smoked over low heat for 10 to 16 hours with hickory or oak wood, producing a bark (a dark, intensely flavoured crust from the smoke, fat, and spice rub) and meat that shreds easily under pressure from the hands. The home oven version cannot replicate the smoke flavour of a proper barbecue pit, but smoked paprika in the rub approximates the character. The key variable is internal temperature: pork shoulder is done when it reaches 90 to 95 C internally, at which point the collagen has fully converted to gelatine and the meat pulls apart without resistance. At 75 C (food-safe) the pork is cooked but not yet pullable; the extra cooking is essential.

recipeTools.notes: A deep roasting tin. A thermometer for the internal temperature.

content.text: The pork shoulder must reach an internal temperature of 90 to 95 C before pulling: at this temperature the collagen in the shoulder has fully converted to gelatine and the meat will shred easily. This is well above the food-safe temperature (75 C) and the cooking time is long because the low oven temperature means the internal temperature rises slowly. Plan for 1 to 1.5 hours per 500 g at 150 C. The resting time after cooking is important: 30 minutes wrapped in foil allows the juices to redistribute and the fibres to relax, making shredding much easier.

items.preparation: bone-in or boneless; score the skin if present

content.text: Mix together all the spices, sugar, salt, and pepper to make the rub. Rub all over the pork shoulder, covering every surface. Leave to marinate in the fridge for at least 2 hours or overnight.

Heat the oven to 150 C / fan 130 C / gas 2. Place the pork in a deep roasting tin. Add 200 ml of water to the tin. Cover tightly with foil. Roast for 5 to 6 hours, basting with the pan juices and apple cider vinegar every 2 hours, until the internal temperature reaches 90 to 95 C and the meat pulls apart easily with two forks.

Remove from the oven and rest, covered with foil, for 30 minutes. Pull the pork apart into shreds using two forks. Skim the fat from the pan juices and pour the juices over the pulled meat. Serve in buns with coleslaw and pickles.
